title: Plain short text where the learner acts
statement: Keep the words a learner reads just before acting to a short plain instruction of at most 14 words, and put any framing in the guide's narration.
example: A cap of 2 sentences and 14 words per field, enforced in code, caught the long task openers in two lessons with one rule.
detail: A reading course's interface rules cap an interaction opener, the text a child reads right before acting, at 2 sentences and 14 words per field, with no theatrics: a plain 'Tap the clues that answer the question' rather than an excited announcement of a clue hunt. Framing belongs in the guide's narration, never on the surface where the child acts. The rule came after the same complaint was raised across several review rounds, and it became a check in code that caught the long openers in two lessons with one rule.

evidence.quote: **An interaction opener is capped at 2 sentences / 14 words per field.** The text a child reads right before ACTING (a hunt's invitation/opening, and by extension any tap-now surface) carries no theatrics
Framing belongs in the guide's narration, never on the acting surface.
clue-hunt-opener length class (now a red-controlled 2-sentence/14-word cap on `hunt.open`, one rule catching both the L4 and L5 instances)
